meta.purpose: Job-description bank for synthetic test-case generation
meta.problem_statement: PS section 6: the test data is fully synthetic; the generation script is committed, and ground-truth labels are fixed in a CSV before any model inference runs.
meta.why_implied_skills_exist: A ground truth built only from skills that appear literally in the JD would be satisfied by literal keyword matching, so condition A would score 100% coverage and the metric would measure nothing. Each responsibility therefore declares the canonical skill it IMPLIES but does not name. Ground truth = named skills UNION implied skills. Conditions B/C can recover the implied half; condition A structurally cannot. That gap IS the lexical-versus-semantic claim being tested.
meta.invariant: A skill declared under `implies` must NOT appear literally anywhere in the JD text. data/synthetic_generator/generate_cases.py asserts this and fails the build if it is violated.
meta.usage: Variants are sorted by named_count; candidate profiles are sorted by strength. Pairing the two orders produces a controlled spread of requirement overlap, including deliberate below-50% hard cases.
meta.privacy: Contains no personal data. All candidate names, emails and phone numbers in profiles.json are fabricated; email domains use the RFC 2606 reserved example.com/example.edu.

terse.opening: {company} is hiring a {title} for our {team} team.
terse.closing: Send your resume and one line on the most relevant thing you have built.

formal.opening: {company} seeks to appoint a {title} within the {team} function. The successful candidate will work alongside senior practitioners and will be expected to demonstrate the following competencies.
formal.closing: Remuneration is commensurate with experience. Shortlisted applicants will be contacted within ten working days.

conversational.opening: We are a small {team} team at {company} and we need a {title} who is comfortable saying what is not working yet.
conversational.requirement_lead: Here is what we actually need you to be good at:
conversational.closing: If that sounds like you, send your resume. We read every one.

verbose.opening: {company} is a fast-growing organisation operating across the region, and we are currently looking to expand our {team} team with a talented and motivated {title} who is eager to develop their career in a supportive and high-performing environment.
verbose.requirement_lead: The role will require the following skills and attributes, which we consider essential for success in this position:
verbose.closing: We look forward to receiving your application and will be in touch regarding next steps should your profile match our requirements for this position.

AI/ML.context: Our applied AI team ships models into products used by real customers, so we care as much about evaluation and monitoring as about training.

responsibilities.text: Prepare the raw rows and document what you excluded and why
Compare candidate approaches against a stated metric instead of shipping the first one that works
Write experiment code that another engineer can re-run and get the same numbers
Put a trained artifact behind a service other teams can call
Explain the limits of a result to non-specialist colleagues in plain language
Turn raw columns into inputs a model can actually use
Keep a container image so the environment is reproducible for everyone

Software Engineering.context: You will work in a small product team where engineers own their code from pull request through to production monitoring.

responsibilities.text: Design and implement service endpoints that other teams consume over HTTP
Write a failing check that reproduces a defect before you fix it
Review changes from teammates and give feedback that improves them
Operate what you build, including responding to the alerts you configured
Break a feature into small increments that can ship independently
Automate the checks that run on every push so a bad change cannot merge
Split a growing application into independently deployable parts when one codebase stops scaling for the team
Query the application data store directly when investigating an issue

Data Analytics.context: You will be the person other teams come to for a number they can defend, which means your working files need to be readable by someone else.

responsibilities.text: Turn a vague business question into a measurable definition
Build and maintain views that the business opens every morning
Work out whether a movement is real or just noise before reporting it
Design a randomised comparison and read it out without stopping early
Move recurring reporting off manual file edits and onto a scheduled job
Reason about the correctness of your own aggregations and window logic
Present a finding to a non-technical audience in two sentences, caveats included

Product Management.context: You will own a small surface area end to end, working with engineering and design, and you will be expected to say what you chose not to build.

responsibilities.text: Articulate the user problem before anyone proposes a solution
Talk to users without leading them toward the answer you want
Sketch the shape of a screen before engineering commits to building it
Order the work and explain what you deliberately deferred this cycle
Decide the one number a change is meant to move, plus the guardrails
Surface a disagreement early and arrive with a recommendation, not a problem statement
Track work items and their status in a shared tracker the whole team can read
Compare what we offer against what a user would otherwise do, including nothing
